source:
# Port of lib/pubid/plateau/parser.rb: PLATEAU Handbook/Technical Report
# #NN[-annex][ edition], plus Annex supplements. Japanese canonical
# edition (第X.Y版) and legacy Latin X.Y both capture the same atom.
#
# Edition 2: every reference inside a captured body is inlined to raw
# terms (a rule reference materializes as a named node in the edition-2
# tree, so only a raw capture binds a scalar span). The base wrapper
# keeps the v1 tree shape and the bindings name the scalar leaves.

grammar PubidPlateau version "0.1.0" edition 2 {
  doc_type = ("Handbook" / "Technical Report") as type
  number = "#" (1*%x30-39) as number
  annex = ("-" / "_") (1*%x30-39) as annex
  edition_part = "第" (1*%x30-39 "." 1*%x30-39) as edition "版"
  edition_latin = (1*%x30-39 "." 1*%x30-39) as edition
  edition = " " (edition_part / edition_latin)
  annex_letter = (%x41-5A) as annex_letter
  annex_supplement = " " "Annex" " " annex_letter
  handbook = "PLATEAU" " " doc_type " " number [annex] [edition]
  technical_report = "PLATEAU" " " doc_type " " number [annex]
  annex_identifier = (handbook / technical_report) as base annex_supplement
  identifier = annex_identifier / handbook / technical_report

  entry identifier: identifier

  test {
    accept "PLATEAU Handbook #3"
    accept "PLATEAU Technical Report #1"
    reject "nonsense"
  }

  bindings identifier {
    # The builder dispatches on base && annex_letter and RE-parses the base
    # subtree recursively (build_annex calls build(parsed[:base])), so base
    # binds uncast — the nested {type, number, annex, edition} hash.
    base -> base (raw)
    type -> type (string)
    number -> number (string)
    annex -> annex (string)
    edition -> edition (string)
    annex_letter -> annex_letter (string)
  }
}
